## Why this matters
Alexander III of Macedon built one of the largest empires of the ancient world before he turned 33 [1]. Knowing how he did it explains why Greek language and culture spread from Egypt to India.

## Early life
Alexander was born in Pella in 356 BCE, the son of King Philip II [1]. As a teenager he was taught by the philosopher Aristotle, who encouraged his interest in science and Homer's epics [2].

## Taking the throne
When Philip was assassinated in 336 BCE, Alexander, then 20, moved quickly to secure the throne and put down revolts in Greece [1, 2].

## Recap
- Alexander was born in 356 BCE and became king at 20.
- Aristotle was his tutor.
- He secured power fast after his father's murder.
